=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel — Buyer-Side Review of Seller Positions

**Context:** Baseline is AUD 24,000,000, debt-free/cash-free, NSW law. Below, each issue is assessed from Wattlebridge's (Buyer's) perspective. "Seller position" summarises their draft; "Buyer should want" states our target; "Recommendation" gives the ask with a one-line reason.

---

**SPA-N-001 — General liability cap**
- **Seller:** 20% of price = AUD 4.8m aggregate cap on general warranty claims.
- **Buyer should want:** Higher cap (commonly 25–50% for private tech deals with concentration risk), especially given Bluefen (~30% revenue) and privacy exposure.
- **Recommendation:** Push cap to 30–50% of price; reason: a 20% cap under-covers a single customer-concentration or data-breach loss that could exceed AUD 4.8m.

**SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket**
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25k; basket AUD 250k (excess-only / deductible, not first-dollar).
- **Buyer should want:** Lower thresholds and ideally a "tipping" basket (recover from first dollar once tripped).
- **Recommendation:** Accept de minimis ~AUD 25k but seek tipping basket at ~AUD 120k (0.5%); reason: a deductible basket forces Buyer to absorb the first AUD 250k of every claim.

**SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months after Completion; and a sweep making all limitations apply to all claims "unless expressly stated."
- **Buyer should want:** 24 months general (to capture at least one full audit cycle); reject the blanket sweep.
- **Recommendation:** 24 months general; delete the "applies to all Claims" sweep; reason: 18 months may close before the first post-Completion audit, and the sweep silently caps tax/fundamental claims.

**SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap/time limits as general ("administrative simplicity").
- **Buyer should want:** Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, ownership of shares) carved out — cap at 100% of price, longer/indefinite period.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; carve out title/capacity at 100% cap, 7-year (or statutory) limit; reason: if the Seller doesn't actually own the shares, Buyer must recover the full purchase price, not 20%.

**SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** Silent; clauses 9.3/12.8/20.5 purport to apply all limitations/exclusive-remedy/non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer should want:** Express carve-out so NO cap, time limit, basket, knowledge qualifier or exclusive-remedy clause applies to fraud, wilful concealment or wilful misconduct.
- **Recommendation:** Insert explicit fraud carve-out from all limitations; reason: NSW courts disfavour contracting out of fraud, but an express carve-out removes doubt and prevents the "all Claims" language from shielding dishonesty.

**SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (as at 5pm 22 Sep 2026) and all public registers — "deemed disclosed."
- **Buyer should want:** Disclosure limited to matters **fairly and specifically** disclosed in sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter; no sweep-up of the whole data room or public records.
- **Recommendation:** Require "fair disclosure" standard + specific Disclosure Letter items only; reason: a blanket data-room/register sweep lets Seller defeat warranties by burying issues in volume.

**SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** Clause 8.3 — no claim for anything Buyer/advisers knew OR that was "discoverable" from data room or public records (constructive knowledge).
- **Buyer should want:** Delete; at most, limit to matters of which specified deal-team individuals had **actual** knowledge.
- **Recommendation:** Strike "discoverable"/constructive knowledge; reason: constructive-knowledge bars shift all diligence risk to Buyer and gut the warranties we are paying for.

**SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent (condition)**
- **Seller:** "Reasonable endeavours"; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of counterparty's written consent — but **no final consent or satisfied conditions in the data room** (Disclosure para 2). Bluefen ≈ AUD 3.6m / 30% revenue.
- **Buyer should want:** Receipt of Bluefen's **unconditional** written consent (with 11.3 conditions satisfied) as a hard Condition Precedent to Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Make unconditional Bluefen consent a CP (not post-Completion); reason: losing a 30%-of-revenue customer on change of control is a material valuation event, not an administrative detail.

**SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** ~AUD 3.2m facility to be released **after** Completion; not repaid, no discharge of security in data room.
- **Buyer should want:** Repayment and discharge of security as a Completion deliverable, funded from proceeds in the funds flow (consistent with debt-free/cash-free).
- **Recommendation:** Require payoff letter + security release at Completion; reason: "release to follow" leaves Buyer owning a company whose assets remain encumbered and contradicts the debt-free/cash-free deal basis.

**SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses (DD-005)**
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 Completion/retention bonuses are "a matter for the Seller," **not itemised in funds flow**; on-costs (payroll tax/super) unstated.
- **Buyer should want:** These are Seller liabilities triggered by the transaction — Seller to bear bonuses **and** on-costs, reflected as a deduction/indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** Specific Seller indemnity for the AUD 420k plus associated super/payroll tax, or price adjustment; reason: transaction-triggered bonuses + on-costs are Seller's cost and otherwise land on Buyer post-Completion.

**SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; "adequate." DD-004 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment (AUD 180k open); no receipt or assignment in data room.
- **Buyer should want:** Confirmation of payment + executed IP assignment pre-Completion, and an indemnity covering **loss of/failure to vest the IP**, not just the fee.
- **Recommendation:** Broaden indemnity to cover failure to acquire SOW3 IP and consequential loss; obtain assignment as CP; reason: if payment isn't cleared the Project Materials IP never vests — the fee amount doesn't compensate for losing the IP itself.

**SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- **Seller:** "Preliminary," "not expected to be material"; ~1,240 individuals' data sent to an unintended address; scope/notification status unresolved.
- **Buyer should want:** Specific indemnity for all costs/liabilities (investigation, OAIC notifiable-data-breach assessment and notification, remediation, regulatory penalties, third-party claims) arising from the incident; Seller to complete investigation pre-Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Uncapped (or separately capped) specific indemnity + pre-Completion investigation update; reason: a possible Notifiable Data Breach under the Privacy Act carries regulatory and penalty exposure that the general cap/basket should not dilute.

**SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals (DD-008/DD-011)**
- **Seller:** Three related renewals AUD 110k each (AUD 330k) are "ordinary-course"; terminability/accrual unstated.
- **Buyer should want:** Clarity on whether renewals are committed/unavoidable; confirmation they are reflected in the debt-free/cash-free and working-capital mechanics (not a hidden committed spend).
- **Recommendation:** Diligence whether these are pre-Completion commitments; if committed, treat as debt-like or adjust price; reason: three "related" renewals read together may be a structured AUD 330k commitment dressed as ordinary opex.

**SPA-N-014 — Category separation**
- **Seller:** Clauses 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply all limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature," and limitations "apply to all Claims unless expressly stated."
- **Buyer should want:** Distinct liability regimes — general warranties vs. fundamental/title vs. tax vs. specific indemnities (Ironquay, privacy) vs. fraud — each with its own cap/time limit.
- **Recommendation:** Replace single-bucket drafting with a separate limitations table per category; reason: collapsing all claims into one regime caps tax, title and indemnity claims at the low general cap/time limit.

**SPA-N-015 — Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title "evidenced" by the DD-012 share register; notes Buyer hasn't verified.
- **Buyer should want:** Full-cap title warranty + Completion deliverables: original share certificates, executed transfers, updated register, director resignations, ASIC confirmation of no charges.
- **Recommendation:** Do not rely on the register alone; require title warranty (100% cap) + Completion title deliverables; reason: the share register is Seller's own record and is not conclusive proof of unencumbered title.

**SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer should want:** Standalone tax deed/indemnity (covering pre-Completion periods, longer limitation aligned to ATO assessment periods) and specific IP warranties (ownership, no infringement, valid licences incl. Ironquay/Mossvale/Bluefen).
- **Recommendation:** Reject folding tax/IP into general regime; require a tax deed and dedicated IP warranties/limitation; reason: tax exposure survives well beyond 18 months and the general cap understates IP/tax risk central to a data-analytics target.

---

## Cross-cutting priorities (negotiation sequencing)
1. **Hard CPs before Completion:** Bluefen unconditional consent (008), Riverlark payoff + discharge (009), Ironquay payment/assignment (011).
2. **Specific indemnities outside the cap/basket:** Privacy incident (012), Ironquay IP (011), DD-005 bonuses + on-costs (010).
3. **Regime structure:** Fundamental/title carve-out (004), fraud carve-out (005), category separation (014), tax deed (016).
4. **Protective drafting:** Fair-disclosure standard (006), delete constructive-knowledge bar (007).
5. **Price/funds-flow integrity:** Ensure Riverlark debt, DD-005 bonuses, and any committed Sandbar spend (013) are correctly captured under debt-free/cash-free — these collectively threaten ~AUD 3.95m of value not reflected in the headline AUD 24m.

---

*This is internal deal-team analysis of the counterparty's draft, not formal legal advice; please have supervising NSW-qualified counsel settle the mark-up. Happy to turn any of the above into redline language or a CP schedule.*
